exercises.hint: For each enrollment, find() the student by id. Skip the ones with no match — that's what INNER JOIN does.
exercises.task: This SQL keeps matches only: students INNER JOIN enrollments ON id = student_id. Build the same 'name - course' pairs with find().

exercises.expectedOutput: ["Morolake - CPRG 304","Morolake - CPRG 307","Tega - CPRG 304","Ama - CPRG 304","Liam - none","Priya - CPRG 307","Noah - none"]
exercises.hint: Loop over students (the left table). For each, collect matching courses; if none matched, use 'none'.
exercises.task: This SQL keeps every left row: students LEFT JOIN enrollments ON id = student_id. Same result in JS — 'none' for students with no courses.

exercises.expectedOutput: ["Morolake - CPRG 304","Morolake - CPRG 307","Tega - CPRG 304","Ama - CPRG 304","Priya - CPRG 307","unknown student - CPRG 304"]
exercises.hint: Loop over enrollments (the right table). When find() returns undefined, use 'unknown student'.
exercises.task: This SQL keeps every right row: students RIGHT JOIN enrollments ON id = student_id. Same in JS — the orphan enrollment gets 'unknown student'.
